# Robots Exclusion Protocol: Key Technical Sections

## User-Agent Line & Product Token Matching (2.2.1)

Product tokens must contain "only uppercase and lowercase letters ("a-z" and "A-Z"), underscores ("_"),
and hyphens ("-")." Crawlers apply "case-insensitive matching to find the group that matches the
product token and then obey the rules of the group."

When multiple groups match the same token, their rules must be "combined into one group and parsed
according to Section 2.2.2." If no explicit match exists, crawlers should "obey the group with a
user-agent line with the "*" value, if present." When no matching group and no wildcard group exist,
"no rules apply."

## Allow/Disallow Rules & Specificity (2.2.2)

Path matching "SHOULD be case sensitive" and "MUST start with the first octet of the path." The
critical precedence rule: "The most specific match found MUST be used. The most specific match is the
match that has the most octets."

If no rules match or a group contains no rules, "the URI is allowed." Additionally, "The /robots.txt
URI is implicitly allowed."

Percent-encoding rules specify: "If a percent-encoded ASCII octet is encountered in the URI, it MUST
be unencoded prior to comparison, unless it is a reserved character."

## Special Characters (2.2.3)

Three characters receive special treatment:
- `#` "Designates a line comment"
- `$` "Designates the end of the match pattern"
- `*` "Designates 0 or more instances of any character"

When matching these literally in URIs, crawlers "SHOULD use "%" encoding."

## Access Method & Error Handling (2.3, 2.3.1)

The robots.txt file location: "scheme:[//authority]/robots.txt"

**Redirects:** Crawlers "SHOULD follow at least five consecutive redirects." Beyond five redirects,
"crawlers MAY assume that the robots.txt file is unavailable."

**Unavailable (4xx):** When receiving 400-499 status codes, "the crawler MAY access any resources
on the server."

**Unreachable (5xx):** On server errors (500-599), "the crawler MUST assume complete disallow." After
30+ days of unavailability, crawlers "MAY assume that the robots.txt file is unavailable."

## Caching (2.4)

Crawlers "SHOULD NOT use the cached version for more than 24 hours, unless the robots.txt file is
unreachable."

## Parsing Limits (2.5)

"The parsing limit MUST be at least 500 kibibytes [KiB]."

## Section 2.2.1: User-Agent Line

Crawlers identify themselves with a "product token" containing only letters, underscores, and hyphens. The token "SHOULD be a substring of the identification string that the crawler sends to the service." Matching is case-insensitive.

When multiple groups match the same product token, their rules merge. If no specific match exists, crawlers "MUST obey the group with a user-agent line with the '*' value, if present."

## Section 2.2.2: Allow and Disallow Lines

Path matching evaluation requires: "The matching SHOULD be case sensitive. The matching MUST start with the first octet of the path. The most specific match found MUST be used."

Non-ASCII characters and reserved characters "MUST be percent-encoded as defined by RFC3986 prior to comparison." Percent-encoded ASCII octets in URIs must be decoded before comparison unless they represent reserved characters.

The example table demonstrates matching behavior for various encoded paths and URIs.

## Section 2.2.3: Special Characters

Three special characters require support:
- **#**: Line comment designator
- **$**: End-of-pattern marker
- **\***: Zero or more character wildcard

For literal matching: "If crawlers match special characters verbatim in the URI, crawlers SHOULD use '%' encoding."

## Section 2.3.1: Access Results

**Successful Access**: Crawlers "MUST follow the parseable rules" after downloading robots.txt.

**Redirects**: "Crawlers SHOULD follow at least five consecutive redirects." Beyond five redirects, robots.txt is presumed unavailable.

**Unavailable Status**: 400-499 status codes mean the crawler "MAY access any resources on the server."

**Unreachable Status**: 500-599 errors mean "the crawler MUST assume complete disallow."

**Parsing Errors**: "Crawlers MUST try to parse each line...Crawlers MUST use the parseable rules."

## Section 2.4: Caching

Crawlers "MAY cache the fetched robots.txt file's contents" and "SHOULD NOT use the cached version for more than 24 hours."

## Section 2.5: Limits

"The parsing limit MUST be at least 500 kibibytes [KiB]."
